scope: Read-only diagnosis of the real npm publish failure; no retry or alternate authentication route.

conclusion.confirmed: The release passed its package gates and signed provenance, then the real npm registry rejected PUT /subswitch with E404. Version0.6.1 is still not published.
conclusion.leadingInference: A publisher credential/account/package-authorization problem is the leading explanation for an existing public package rejecting this write. The visible E404 is not specific enough to identify expired token, revocation, wrong token identity/scope or 2FA policy. No exact cause is proven.
conclusion.confidence: High for failure boundary and unpublished status; moderate for authentication/authorization category; unknown for exact credential or policy defect.
conclusion.remainingBlocker: Dean must inspect the publisher-side credential metadata/package policy or have npm support explain this rejection. The current denied write must not be bypassed.

confirmedFacts.fact: Release workflow at the exact tag equals current-main workflow. It uses the expected registry, npm publish --provenance --access public, and NODE_AUTH_TOKEN from repository NPM_TOKEN. The pinned official setup-node source supports this wiring.
Install, tag/package version guard, lockfile version guard, Check, Build and Smoke all succeeded. The publish hook also ran973 tests with0fail before prepack.

Published-attempt package metadata is subswitch@0.6.1,60files,SHA1 8bf02b981d91a18051a96d0087be50cac42a0106, matching the reviewed release candidate. Repository points to dean0x/subswitch and private is false; no publishConfig override.
Log reports provenance signed and placed in Sigstore transparency log before the registry PUT failed. That does not establish npm package-write authorization.
Actual registry response is E404,404 Not Found,PUT https://registry.npmjs.org/subswitch. No explicit expired/revoked token message, E401, E403 or EOTP appears in this failed publish-step log.

Public unauthenticated registry GET returns200 for subswitch; latest remains0.6.0 and0.6.1 is absent. Public maintainer and last successful publisher names are dean0x. This does not identify the principal of the current CI token.

Repository secret name NPM_TOKEN exists, last metadata update2026-10-08T17:44:35Z. Its existence/date and masked run variable do not establish token type, identity, expiry, scope, IP allowance or 2FA capability. Secret values were not read.
Runner used Node22.23.3/npm10.9.9. The npm docs require CLI11.5.1+ for trusted publishing, so success of GitHub OIDC/Sigstore does not make this old CLI a trusted npm publisher.

hypotheses.cause: Expired, revoked, malformed or otherwise invalid NPM_TOKEN
hypotheses.whyNotConfirmed: No token metadata/value inspected and no explicit expiration/revocation notice. The GitHub secret update date is not the token expiration date.

hypotheses.cause: Token belongs to a different account, lacks package write access, omits subswitch, or account lost publishing permission
hypotheses.whyNotConfirmed: Public package ownership does not reveal CI token identity or grant. No authenticated permission probe was made.

hypotheses.cause: Publishing 2FA/package policy, token automation capability, stage-only or IP restrictions
hypotheses.whyNotConfirmed: Private policy/credential metadata is unknown. No specific OTP/forbidden error is shown; stage-only tokens are documented to produce E_STAGE_REQUIRED, which was not observed.
Tagged metadata, guards, public package URL and successful package gates match. A new version being absent before publication is expected and does not justify renaming it or moving registries.

This workflow uses the token path on npm10.9.9, below documented OIDC publishing minimum. No trusted-publisher configuration was inspected; automatically switching authentication would be outside this assignment.

hypotheses.cause: Registry-side transient problem or undocumented rejection
hypotheses.status: Cannot exclude from one generic response
hypotheses.whyNotConfirmed: Only the visible404 body is available, without server-side diagnostics. If credential metadata and policy are correct, npm support is the supported next diagnostic step, not repeated blind publishes.

minimalSupportedRemedy.recommendation: First inspect existing publisher-side metadata. If the token is unusable or has the wrong authorized grant, replace it within the existing permitted token publishing method; no source/version/tag/workflow change is indicated by current evidence.
userActions: Dean signs in to npm as the authorized subswitch publisher and checks Access Tokens metadata plus the package publishing-access policy: validity, selected package, publish permission, required automation 2FA capability and any IP restrictions. Do not paste or reveal token values.

If replacement is needed and package policy permits token publishing, create a supported granular token limited to subswitch, with Read and write (publish and stage), a suitable short expiration, and Bypass 2FA for this noninteractive release where permitted. Do not broaden package/account policies or runner IP grants automatically.

Dean updates the existing NPM_TOKEN repository Actions secret directly in GitHub Settings > Secrets and variables > Actions. Tell the coordinator only that it is updated; never send its value through chat or diagnostic output.

If the package forbids tokens or valid metadata does not explain the rejection, stop and tell the coordinator. Do not weaken 2FA policy. A separately authorized trusted-publishing migration or npm support investigation is required.
minimalSupportedRemedy.retryBoundary: Only after the publisher-side issue is resolved and the coordinator has authority for another real write should it recheck the registry and decide whether to rerun the existing tagged workflow. No new version/tag deletion is indicated while0.6.1 remains absent. No rerun or publish was performed here.
minimalSupportedRemedy.longTerm: npm recommends OIDC trusted publishing and documents direct bypass-2FA token publishing retirement in January2027. That migration is separately tracked; it is not authorization to route around this rejected token publish.

officialSources.title: npm: About access tokens
officialSources.supports: Only granular tokens are currently supported; token rights are bounded by account permissions and may be scoped, expiring, IP-limited or stage-only. Direct token publishing remains supported now but is documented to end in January2027.

officialSources.title: npm: Creating and viewing access tokens
officialSources.supports: The npm website lets the publisher create a package-scoped granular token, select publishing rights, expiration and automation 2FA behavior. Organization-management access alone does not grant package publishing rights.

officialSources.title: npm: CI/CD authentication
officialSources.supports: npm recommends trusted publishing for CI/CD. The existing token method uses a minimally scoped publishing credential and may require automation 2FA capability; store its value in CI secrets.

officialSources.title: npm: Publishing 2FA requirements
officialSources.supports: Package policy may forbid all tokens. A permitted noninteractive token publisher requires the appropriate 2FA capability. Do not change a strict package policy to get past this failure.

officialSources.title: npm: Generating provenance statements
officialSources.supports: The official token/provenance workflow uses id-token permission, registry setup and NODE_AUTH_TOKEN from an npm secret. Signing provenance is separate from an accepted registry publish.

officialSources.title: npm: Trusted publishing
officialSources.supports: Trusted publishing needs npm CLI>=11.5.1 and an explicitly authorized package/workflow trust relationship; id-token permission alone is insufficient. Current npm10.9.9 is below that minimum.

officialSources.title: GitHub: Using secrets in Actions
officialSources.supports: Repository Actions secrets are managed under Settings, Secrets and variables, Actions; workflows receive them through the secrets context.

officialSources.title: Pinned official actions/setup-node authentication implementation
officialSources.supports: Pinned action writes a registry auth reference to NODE_AUTH_TOKEN and exports NPM_CONFIG_USERCONFIG. The tagged workflow supplies that variable at the publish step.
